summary: Initial procurement and legal intake focusing on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing approval path, and evidence for security/compliance. Customer prefers VPC/dedicated options for PHI, asked for SOC2 and KMS details. Team agreed next steps to circulate redlines, share compliance artifacts, and schedule pilot kickoff.
topics: Pricing approval process and reserved capacity options
Security artifacts: SOC2, encryption, KMS, SSO
transcript:
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving time. We're expecting 45ish minutes to run through the procurement ask and DPA/MSA redline items.
00:10 Priya (Procurement): Thanks, Maya. Quick intro: I'm Priya; I'll be shepherding procurement. Mark from legal is here, and Elena will ask sec questions. Tom's on the platform side.
00:18 Mark (Legal): Hi all. We got the standard MSA but with some Helix-specific edits. We'll flag indemnity, liability cap, and data residency.
00:28 Chris (Redwood SE): Great — quick note: we have a dedicated capacity offering and a private VPC deployment pattern that most health customers use for PHI. We also have KMS integrations and HSM options.
00:40 Elena (SecEng): When you say KMS integrations, what key management models? Customer-managed keys? We need to know if Redwood can use our cloud KMS or if keys are held by Redwood.
00:54 Chris: We support customer-managed keys via standard KMS providers, and we offer envelope encryption. For on-prem or VPC, you can bring keys; for hosted there is an option to use our KMS with bring-your-own-key rotation.
01:10 Tom (Platform): Also curious about audit logs — retention, granularity, and whether token-level traces are exportable to our SIEM.
01:22 Jordan (CSM): Yes, we can stream audit logs; retention tiers are configurable. We'll share a diagram of what events are available.
01:31 Mark: On the MSA, liability cap needs to be aligned with our enterprise risk — currently your standard caps are lower than our policy. We will propose language around carve-outs for gross negligence and IP infringement.
01:44 Maya: Understood. We typically have a negotiated cap tied to annual fees — for Dedicated it's a different band. We'll flag that in the annotated MSA and propose a path.
01:56 Priya: Procurement timeline — we need pricing packaged in the format procurement uses: list price, committed spend options, and PO terms. Who owns the pricing spreadsheet?
02:06 Maya: I'll send the pricing worksheet. We can show pay-as-you-go vs reserved capacity examples — committed units/month with discounts.
02:15 Priya: Is there any requirement around market-competitive benchmarking? Our committee asks for 3 vendor comps.
02:22 Maya: Customers often include cost/TCO slides — we can provide a concise comparison of cost per 1M tokens and dedicated pool unit economics. Note: numbers vary with quantization and batching.
02:35 Elena: Regarding DPA — how is PHI treated? Are you willing to sign a DPA that enumerates processing of PHI under the HIPAA business associate style protections?
02:47 Chris: We don't provide a HIPAA BAA by default in the hosted tier; for healthcare customers we recommend Private or Dedicated, and we can have a DPA with PHI clauses, plus a technical architecture to minimize data exposure. We'll confirm legal language.
03:00 Mark: We'll need data residency guarantees for EU/US; also subprocessor list. Please provide current subprocessor names and SOC details.
03:10 Maya: We'll share the subprocessor list and SOC2 Type II report. Chris will upload the security artifacts.
03:18 Speaker 3 (auto): I think there's a doc link posted in chat, drive/redwood/security-pack-2025.
03:25 Tom: A procurement-specific question: our finance team requires invoice net-60 and certain tax clauses. Does Redwood have flexibility on payment terms for committed contracts?
03:36 Maya: For committed reserved capacity contracts we can be flexible on payment terms; net-30 is default, but we can escalate for enterprise customers to net-60 on annual prepay. We'll put options in the pricing sheet.
03:46 Mark: About SLAs — what does your uptime coverage look like for Dedicated? We need 99.9 at minimum for production workloads. Also latency SLOs for p95 on 4k token requests.
03:59 Chris: SLA for Dedicated pools is typically 99.9. Latency SLOs are a function of model and sequence length; p95 for typical 2k token generation we target 300-800ms depending on model. For longer sequences p95 increases. We'll provide benchmark profiles and the model catalog.
04:20 Elena: Does Redwood support automatic failover across regions for dedicated pools? We need cross-region redundancy for DR.
04:31 Chris: We support policy-driven routing and cross-region fallback, though Dedicated cross-region active-active for the same reserved pool may require additional setup. We can document options.
04:42 Priya: Okay — procurement also flags cybersecurity insurance and evidence of controls. We'll ask for vendor security questionnaire.
04:50 Maya: We'll return a completed vendor questionnaire and SOC2 report. We'll also include contact for our security lead.
04:58 Mark: A lot of our legal redlines are around indemnity and data breach notification windows. We usually ask for 72-hour breach notification.
05:07 Chris: We can commit to 72 hours for breaches affecting customer data; we'll confirm the exact wording in the DPA.
05:15 Tom: Does Redwood have a standard playbook for incident response and runbooks we can review?
05:22 Jordan: Yes — we have incident response summaries and runbooks; we'll share an executive summary and a redacted runbook if needed.
05:30 Speaker 2 (auto): Also note — some transcription glitches here: 'KV cache' came through as 'k v cash' in earlier notes.
05:36 Maya: Good call-out. We'll be mindful of technical terms in the draft.
05:40 Priya: Pricing approvals — our committee requires procurement + legal + platform sign-off. We expect a final review meeting after we get the redlines and compliance artifacts. Can we get a week turnaround?
05:52 Maya: Yes, our timeline is: send redlines this week, SOC2 + security artifacts early next week, then reconvene with your committee mid-April.
06:03 Mark: Any third-party subprocessors that we should be particularly mindful of? Do you use any offshored teams for support or model tuning?
06:12 Chris: Support is primarily in-region; we do not use offshore teams for customer data handling. Model tuning is handled by the platform; we can provide details on any third parties used for telemetry processing.
06:26 Elena: Encryption at rest and in transit — should we assume AES-256 and TLS1.2+? Also want details on key rotation cadence.
06:36 Chris: Yes, AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit. Key rotation cadence configurable; default 90 days if managed by us, and customer-managed keys can be rotated per their policy.
06:50 Priya: On the MSA redlines — we'll push for a 12-month warranty and trial SLAs with acceptance criteria for pilot outcomes. We need measurable success metrics to unlock procurement.
07:02 Jordan: For the pilot we'll define acceptance metrics: throughput, p95 latency, and qualitative quality checks on sample prompts. We'll draft a pilot success criteria template.
07:14 Mark: There's also a clause around export controls and restricted data classification; add that to the exchange.
07:22 Maya: We'll annotate the DPA and MSA on those lines. We'll also include a suggested liability cap language for negotiation.
07:30 Tom: Can you provide a breakdown of costs if we choose Dedicated pool with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs vs hosted high-throughput? We need per-month run rates and how burst is charged.
07:42 Maya: Yes, the pricing workbook will show dedicated pool sizing estimates, committed discounts, and burst pricing. For hosted we provide per-token pricing with concurrency limits.
07:52 Mark: We're likely to request a small carve-out for the liability cap for IP indemnity. Expect that in the redlines.
07:58 Maya: Understood. We'll highlight where we can accept exceptions and where we have to escalate to executive legal.
08:06 Priya: Procurement question — will Redwood accept a PO against the master agreement with monthly invoices or do you require award-first?
08:16 Maya: We accept POs under the MSA. For committed reserved capacity we typically do a signed SOW + PO. We'll outline options in the pricing doc.
08:26 Elena: About data deletion — if we stop service, what's the retention period and can you purge all customer data on request?
08:35 Chris: We have a data deletion policy — default is retain for 30 days after contract termination unless otherwise agreed. We can lower retention or provide immediate purge under DPA clauses for PHI.
08:47 Mark: We'll propose stricter deletion timelines for PHI and audit evidence of deletion.
08:54 Jordan: We'll include a logging proof process and delete confirmation artifact in the runbook.
09:02 Maya: Okay, quick recap — action items: we'll circulate annotated MSA/DPA, Chris uploads SOC2 and infra diagrams, Jordan drafts pilot success criteria and runbook, Helix provides legal must-haves and procurement timeline. Any final questions?
09:18 Priya: One small ask — can you include a point of contact for billing disputes?
09:24 Maya: Yes, I'll add billing contact and escalation path.
09:28 Mark: Also please attach your subprocessor list and if possible a redacted subproc contract template.
09:36 Chris: We'll see what we can share; some subproc agreements are redacted, but we'll provide names and SOC status.
09:42 Speaker 1 (auto): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
09:48 Maya: Thanks all — we'll aim to get the doc bundle to you by EOD Thursday.
09:53 Priya: Appreciate it. We'll look to reconvene mid-April after internal review.
09:58 End of recording.
